correctness.rationale: For any admissible ultrametric extension vector the least distance j and a chosen nearest parameter b force f(a)=max(j,d(a,b)); conversely this defines a valid vector. This bijects complete one-types with all radius-j balls, graded by cardinality. Choose m distinct partitions of size t; their unordered selection determines pairwise nonisometric trees; at fixed outer-ball sizes the polynomial has at most p(n) possible level-one histograms. The injection from subsets of {2,...,k+1} gives p(t)>=2^k>=n^2, binomial and partition Euler-product estimates give F(n)>=exp(m log n-pi sqrt(2n/3)), and t=O(log^2 n) implies exp(Omega(n/log n)). All assumptions and edge conditions (n>=t, residual r<t) are stated. The separately implemented direct distance-vector counting algorithm confirmed the correspondence for all 220 ultrametric isometry types through size 7; all 223 order-8 hierarchies were grouped by signature. Numerical data are verification only, not the asymptotic proof.

originality.rationale: An exact all-size lower bound of exp(Omega(n/log n)) is established for fibers of the complete nearest-distance/nearest-count type polynomial. The previously established ball/type correspondence and five-point nonrigidity are excluded from the novelty claim. The earlier published all-arity type-spectrum theorem says that tuple-type counts depend on numbers of balls and gives a five-point ambiguity even with levelwise sizes supplied; it does not state or imply this quantitative rate without the new distinct-partition construction. A published two-round colour-refinement reconstruction theorem has a strictly stronger, vertex-correlated invariant, and Mémoli–Zhou give a five-point barcode witness, not an asymptotic count. Actual searches and inspected relevant material yielded no decisive coverage. Residual risk: historical multilevel-tree histogram literature could contain an equivalent asymptotic counting bound.
residual_risks: Equivalent exponential lower bounds could be implicit or explicit in unindexed combinatorial literature on multilevel dendrogram histograms or degree sequences.
Only relevant regions, not all pages, of long primary sources were inspected; their whole-document absence of a covering result is not certified.

value.rationale: Exact type-spectrum inversion is naturally motivated by which information named finite parameters retain. The theorem gives an all-n quantitative rate for the largest isometry fiber of a mathematically natural two-variable distribution, retaining all per-radius ball-size partitions but erasing nesting. The exponential nonreconstruction is a substantial structural obstruction stronger than a finite witness, with a constructive method and explicit finite-n lower bound; no downstream theorem is required.
